Scene art / walkable ground agreement contract
Godot autoload + JSON-content architecture borrowed from the example doc

nodes.label: Passport Stamps as Proof of Visit
nodes.norm_label: passport stamps as proof of visit

nodes.label: The Atlas (map of the internet)
nodes.rationale: Reframes the internet as a explorable map of four islands rather than an abstract network, so a 7-12 year old has a spatial mental model to travel through.

nodes.label: Walkable 2D realm scene
nodes.rationale: Each step (story, decision, mini-game, rule) relocates the interaction pin and mutates the scene, so progress is felt as physical change in the world rather than a page advancing.

nodes.label: No fail state / warm redirect
nodes.rationale: Picking the unsafe option hands the decision straight back with a warm Comet redirect; no dead ends, no timers, and no visible score, so the child is never punished for exploring the wrong answer.

nodes.label: scene_y = world_y x 2.8 coordinate conversion
nodes.rationale: Scene art (560x280 viewBox in RealmArt.jsx) and the walkable band (0-100 world units in data/realms.js) live in different coordinate systems with nothing enforcing agreement; the 2.8 scalar is the only bridge, so both authoring rules hang off it.

nodes.label: Rule 1: solid ground across the whole walkable band
nodes.rationale: Art changes after the safe choice, so ground must hold in both moods; breaking this produced a campfire burning on open water and a Traveler walking across a bog.
nodes.norm_label: rule 1: solid ground across the whole walkable band

nodes.label: Rule 2: nothing solid floats above the band
nodes.rationale: World.jsx draws the Traveler over the scene unconditionally with no depth sorting, so any prop above the band makes the player walk in front of something they should pass behind.
nodes.norm_label: rule 2: nothing solid floats above the band

nodes.label: #art scene contact sheet (dev-only)
nodes.rationale: Overlays the walkable band and every hotspot on all four realms in both moods at once, which is faster at catching ground-rule violations than walking to all sixteen corners by hand.

nodes.label: No image assets: all art is SVG shapes
nodes.rationale: Every character and scene is built from SVG shapes and fonts are self-hosted via @fontsource, so the built site makes no external requests.
nodes.norm_label: no image assets: all art is svg shapes

nodes.label: requestAnimationFrame walk loop with clamped timestep
nodes.rationale: Pauses in a background tab and resumes with a clamped timestep so the Traveler never teleports; automated tests see a frozen Traveler because browsers throttle rAF to zero in hidden tabs, which is a harness artifact not a bug.
nodes.norm_label: requestanimationframe walk loop with clamped timestep

nodes.label: Step panel portalled to body
nodes.rationale: .fold animates a perspective()/rotateY() transform, which makes it a containing block, so a position:fixed scrim inside resolves against the realm card instead of the viewport; anything full-screen must be portalled out.

nodes.label: Sticky panel action rows
nodes.rationale: .center and .panel-actions stick to the bottom of the panel because a long story beat would otherwise push the only way forward below the fold, and a child who cannot see the button is stuck.

nodes.label: Deviation: walkable world replaces card navigation
nodes.rationale: design.md section 5 specified point-and-click cards with no moving character; changed on request so realms are walked, though mini-games remain tap puzzles.
nodes.norm_label: deviation: walkable world replaces card navigation

nodes.label: Deviation: real Vite app instead of single-file artifact
nodes.rationale: design.md section 9 assumed an artifact (Tailwind, no localStorage), but section 7 had already flagged persistence as the follow-up once the base game existed.
nodes.norm_label: deviation: real vite app instead of single-file artifact

nodes.label: Deviation: Balance as a third mini-game component
nodes.rationale: design.md section 6 lists only Sort and Spot, but 'Balance the Day' is a scale rather than two bins, so it got its own component while reusing Sort's exact tap-to-place controls so there is no new control to learn.
nodes.norm_label: deviation: balance as a third mini-game component

nodes.label: Concept summary: single-sitting Atlas journey
nodes.rationale: One 20-30 minute sitting for ages 7-12; each realm teaches one cyber wellness topic via story beat, branching decision, and a hands-on mini-game, tracked by stamps in a passport journal.

nodes.label: Field-journal / passport metaphor
nodes.rationale: Grounds the whole product so the internet feels like a nature reserve visited with a guide and a notebook, worth exploring thoughtfully, rather than a void to fear or a screen to be babysat through; every badge is a physical-feeling ink stamp, not a digital trophy.

nodes.label: Rejected trope: neon-cyberspace-on-black
nodes.rationale: Dark backgrounds, glowing circuits and matrix grids read as scary or hacker-coded, working against the message that the internet is a place kids can explore safely.

nodes.label: Rejected trope: warm-cream-and-serif AI default
nodes.rationale: Flattens personality and does not fit an energetic kids' product.

nodes.label: Color token system (paper, ink, realm accents)
nodes.rationale: Each realm accent is used only inside that realm's screens and stamp while hub and shared UI stay ink/paper, so the four colors read as distinct regions of a map rather than a rainbow UI; ink is deep fountain-pen navy and never pure black.
nodes.norm_label: color token system (paper, ink, realm accents)

nodes.label: Type system: Display / Body / Stamp-Label
nodes.rationale: Baloo 2 or Fredoka for display at large sizes only, Nunito body at 18-20px for age-appropriate readability, and a monospace (Space Mono / IBM Plex Mono) confined to stamps, pins and badge labels because that is what sells the passport-ink signature; it must not leak into body copy.

nodes.label: Signature element: the ink stamp badge
nodes.rationale: Irregular-edged circle in realm accent with an arced monospace label, landing at a rotation randomized once per session so the journal feels hand-stamped not templated; it is the one recurring wow moment, so the rest of the UI stays quiet to avoid competing.
nodes.norm_label: signature element: the ink stamp badge

nodes.label: Screen flow: gate to Atlas to realms to finale
nodes.rationale: Realms complete in any order and return to the hub; the finale unlocks only once all four stamps are earned.
nodes.norm_label: screen flow: gate to atlas to realms to finale

nodes.label: Decision point pattern (two choice cards, no dead end)
nodes.rationale: Selecting the unsafe option shows a brief warm redirect and lets the child pick again, so there is no wrong-answer dead end and nothing punishes or scares.
nodes.norm_label: decision point pattern (two choice cards, no dead end)

nodes.label: Sort mechanic (two labeled bins)
nodes.rationale: Mechanics are deliberately kept to two and reused across realms with different content so kids do not have to learn new controls each time.

nodes.label: Page-fold transition
nodes.rationale: Reinforces the journal metaphor between hub and realm screens; kept to ~250-300ms and respects prefers-reduced-motion.

nodes.label: Component inventory for the React build
nodes.norm_label: component inventory for the react build

nodes.label: State & data model (travelerName, currentScreen, realmProgress)
nodes.rationale: All state lives in useState/useReducer in memory because artifacts cannot use browser storage; persistence via window.storage is flagged as worth adding once the base game is built, not before.

nodes.label: Accessibility & kid-safety UX notes
nodes.rationale: Min ~48px tap targets for a touch-first product, no timers or fail states or score pressure, text-equivalent instruction lines, color never the only signal, and no real personal data beyond an in-session first name.

nodes.label: Technical constraints (artifact-era)
nodes.rationale: Single-file React artifact with Tailwind core utilities only, no localStorage per artifact rules, lucide-react icons, no framer-motion, and no external image assets.

nodes.label: Scene construction (section 9a): art must agree with walkable ground
nodes.rationale: Making realms walkable introduced a constraint the card design never had; failures already caught this way include a bonfire and friends burning on open water, a bog with no bank, and a Keeper hovering twenty units above the ground - it reads immediately as broken to a child.
nodes.norm_label: scene construction (section 9a): art must agree with walkable ground

nodes.label: Motion budget: two spent moments only
nodes.rationale: Animation is spent only on the stamp thunk and the page-fold transition; everything else uses ~150ms opacity/scale changes so nothing bouncy competes with the two signature moments.
nodes.norm_label: motion budget: two spent moments only

nodes.label: Godot 4 port design doc
nodes.rationale: Merges this repo's actual content and visual system with the engineering patterns (Autoloads, JSON content, node-per-mechanic, performance discipline) of an uploaded Godot example doc, while discarding that doc's curriculum and grade-banded level concepts.

nodes.label: Revision note: replace bin-heavy mechanics
nodes.rationale: The original draft kept Sort/Sort/Spot/Balance, three of which are variations on 'put things in a bin' - flat once it is an actual game instead of a web form; so a platformer and a stepping-stone run were borrowed from the example doc while Bully Bog's Sort and Balance Bay's Balance stayed.

nodes.label: Decision: stay 2D, not 3D
nodes.rationale: Two independent reasons: the example doc's performance section rules out 3D for this audience/hardware (target the oldest laptop in the room), and this game's identity IS 2D paper-journal illustration, so 3D would fight the 'internet as a place worth exploring' rationale. Extra depth comes from parallax layers, an ink-bleed shader, and capped GPUParticles2D instead.

nodes.label: Principle 1: no fail state (Godot)
nodes.rationale: Decision scenes never queue_free() on a wrong pick; they swap the dialogue label and re-enable the choice buttons.

nodes.label: Principle 2: the mechanic is the lesson
nodes.rationale: Winning must require doing the safe behaviour, not just be themed around it - hence the platformer meter is built from real character-type mixing and the river stones are the actual scam scenarios, not decoration around an unrelated jumping puzzle.
nodes.norm_label: principle 2: the mechanic is the lesson

nodes.label: Principle 3: four mechanics, one per realm
nodes.rationale: Deliberately trades design.md's 'fewer controls to learn' for 'each realm feels distinct', judged worth it once this is a real game rather than a form.
nodes.norm_label: principle 3: four mechanics, one per realm

nodes.label: Principle 4: nothing is a villain
nodes.rationale: Keeper Vex, the Fog and the Glimmer are misguided-not-malicious; the dialogue tone must survive the port verbatim.

nodes.label: Principle 5: no login, no data collection
nodes.rationale: Only a first name held in memory today; Godot save data must stay local-only to keep this intact.
nodes.norm_label: principle 5: no login, no data collection

nodes.label: Realm anatomy (Realm.tscn node layout)
nodes.rationale: Every realm is one .tscn with the same internal state machine driven by JSON content instead of hardcoded dialogue; Bully Bog and Balance Bay keep the four-phase shape while Passworld and Privacy Peaks fold decision into the mini-game.

nodes.label: RealmState machine (idle to story to game to rule to stamped)
nodes.norm_label: realmstate machine (idle to story to game to rule to stamped)

nodes.label: Walk system port (useWalker.js to CharacterBody2D)
nodes.rationale: The current walker is already exactly Godot's CharacterBody2D pattern: _physics_process replaces the rAF loop, Input.get_vector() replaces the KEY_DIRS table, and a clicked point sets a target Vector2 mirroring walkTo(); 0-100 world units stay resolution-independent with one scalar per realm.

nodes.label: Hotspots as Area2D stops
nodes.rationale: Each realm's four named stops become Area2D nodes with a label and action verb; RealmState enables only the hotspot relevant to the current phase, the same gating RealmScreen does in React today.

nodes.label: Password Fortress platformer (Passworld)
nodes.rationale: A strength meter fills only from a mix of letter/number/symbol tiles, and decoy tiles shaped like weak passwords (123456, password) are easy to reach but reduce the meter - teaching 'looks like a password, isn't a strong one' the way the old Sort game's bins taught 'looks shareable, isn't'. A patrolling hacker knocks the player back to the section start: momentum lost, not a life.

nodes.label: Cross the Fog stepping-stone run (Privacy Peaks)
nodes.rationale: Merges the old decision card and the separate Clear the Fog spot game into one phase; the six existing messages map one-to-one onto six stones, and two of them are genuinely fine so the run does not train 'every stranger message is a trap'. Wrong picks wobble the stone and produce a soft splash, not a drowning, then re-offer the same stone.
nodes.norm_label: cross the fog stepping-stone run (privacy peaks)

nodes.label: Clear the Water sort (Bully Bog, unchanged)
nodes.rationale: Immediate per-item feedback rather than end-of-round scoring, matching design.md's no-score-pressure rule.
nodes.norm_label: clear the water sort (bully bog, unchanged)

nodes.label: Balance the Day (Balance Bay, unchanged)
nodes.rationale: 6 slots filled from 10 cards with no single correct split - only all-screen or no-screen trip a verdict, and a level mix reads as 'that's the whole trick'.

nodes.label: Content lives in JSON, not GDScript
nodes.rationale: Called the example doc's strongest idea and taken wholesale, so dialogue and realm bounds are authored data rather than code.
nodes.norm_label: content lives in json, not gdscript

nodes.label: journey_manager autoload
nodes.rationale: Holds traveler name, current screen and the realm_progress dictionary carried over unchanged from design.md section 7; set up first so every realm scene can read what has been earned without re-wiring signals scene-to-scene.

nodes.label: Local FileAccess save system
nodes.rationale: A Godot build is a real client and can persist for free, so a small local JSON save at user:// is framed as a genuine upgrade from the port rather than scope creep - it stores nothing beyond the first name already collected, keeping Principle 5 intact.

nodes.label: Visual system ported token-for-token
nodes.rationale: design.md section 3 tokens map onto Theme panel background, Theme font colors, per-realm realm_accent export vars, and three DynamicFont resources - explicitly ported rather than reinterpreted.

nodes.label: Ink stamp badge in Godot (Path2D arc label, baked jitter)
nodes.rationale: Per-vertex circle jitter is baked once rather than randomized at runtime, and the +/-6 degree rotation is set once on stamp-earned and never re-rolled, to match design.md's 'randomized once per session'.
nodes.norm_label: ink stamp badge in godot (path2d arc label, baked jitter)

nodes.label: Godot motion budget (two moments)
nodes.rationale: Godot has no direct prefers-reduced-motion equivalent, so a skippable/instant page-fold would need a manual settings toggle if it matters enough to add.

nodes.label: HTML5 export as primary distribution target
nodes.rationale: This is a browser game today with no offline/classroom requirement in the repo docs, unlike the example doc's school-laptop .exe scenario; native export stays an easy later addition but nothing should be built around requiring it.
nodes.norm_label: html5 export as primary distribution target

nodes.label: Suggested build order (cheapest mechanic first)
nodes.rationale: Sequenced by mechanical complexity: Bully Bog goes first (not Passworld) because a plain Control-based Sort validates the walk system, hotspot gating, dialogue cards, stamp thunk and page-fold at lowest risk; the platformer is last because it is the only mechanic needing real collision, camera follow and game-feel playtesting.

nodes.label: Open questions (save, audio, milestone scope, difficulty, stone count)
nodes.rationale: Explicitly left undecided: persistence vs session-only parity, audio vs silence, vertical slice vs all four realms, a difficulty pass for the platformer, and whether six river stones exceed the example doc's 4-5 scenario budget.
nodes.norm_label: open questions (save, audio, milestone scope, difficulty, stone count)
